compareDisposition.rationale: No distinct two-source pairing adds more than this passage and its existing Scripture connections.

observations.body: The LORD promises a messenger, warns Israel to hear his voice, names opposition to enemies, forbids other gods, promises provision, and describes gradual possession without covenant with land inhabitants.
observations.label: A messenger, gradual conquest, and guarded allegiance

observations.body: A messenger, gradual conquest, and guarded allegiance belongs to covenant ordinances in the Sinai trail.
observations.label: Where this sits

observations.body: Exodus 23:20–33 supplies core evidence for the event’s developing sequence.
observations.label: Within the Sinai event

observations.body: The ordinances follow the Ten Words and apply them through concrete cases, but they are not identical to the Decalogue.
observations.label: Reading boundary

payload.posture: Read Exodus 23:20–33 as its own source before carrying it into the wider Sinai trail.
payload.tension: A messenger, gradual conquest, and guarded allegiance belongs to the covenant ordinances movement, but its part in the event must remain distinct from the surrounding speech, response, breach, and renewal.
payload.title: A messenger, gradual conquest, and guarded allegiance
